name: Achan
overview: Achan was a male member of the tribe of Judah known for taking forbidden items from the city of Jericho, an act that violated God's command. This transgression is recorded in Joshua 7:1. There are no additional notes providing further context about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Achan means 'troubler,' reflecting the trouble he caused through his disobedience. He is also referred to as Achar, meaning 'trouble,' which underscores the consequences of his actions as noted in 1 Chronicles 2:7. Neither name was given by God, but both highlight the impact of his sin.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Achan as the son of Carmi, as stated in Joshua 7:1. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Achan's significance lies in his violation of God's command by taking forbidden spoils from Jericho, which brought trouble upon Israel. His act of disobedience serves as a sobering example of the seriousness of sin and its consequences within the covenant community. His story emphasizes the need for holiness and obedience to God's instructions in the life of His people.
